answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through proof of burn, requiring nodes to destroy tokens to register valid IDs. Instead of allowing a fleeting zephyr of automated replicas to dilute routing tables, the network enforces an escalating dune of burned capital. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of sacrificing liquid financial assets per identity, leaving an auditable cryptographic ember of destroyed value. However, this barrier excludes resource-constrained open-source agents.
